reconcile.note: The Geneva annotators read John's denial as answering the delegation's own notion of Elijah, not the sense in which Christ affirms it.

discrepancy.note: Strauss finds it improbable John's Gospel would deny the Elias identity so flatly if its author knew the Synoptic tradition affirming it.

quotes.text: In John i. 21, when the emissaries of the Sanhedrim ask, “Art thou Elias?” the Baptist declines this dignity… Nevertheless it appears improbable that if the fourth Evangelist had been familiar with the idea of the Baptist as a second Elias, he would have put into his mouth so direct a negative.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), pt. II, ch. VI, on John 1:21.

sides.snippet: If you are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, who is to come.
sides.verseText: If you are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, who is to come.

sides.snippet: They asked him, \"What then? Are you Elijah?\" He said, \"I am not.\" \"Are you the Prophet?\" He answered, \"No.\"
sides.verseText: They asked him, \"What then? Are you Elijah?\" He said, \"I am not.\" \"Are you the Prophet?\" He answered, \"No.\"
